question: Why does the Bank of Canada put security features on banknotes?
generated_answer:
You may not think about it this way, but cash is a technology. You might ask, why does the Bank change the design of banknotes? The short answer is to make them more secure. With time, new technologies, such as better scanners and graphic software, make it easier to counterfeit banknotes. To protect the banknotes, we design and include enhanced security features to make them harder to counterfeit. We also collaborate with our partners in law enforcement and the cash-handling industry to encourage counterfeit detection and to deter counterfeiting. We want to get counterfeits out of circulation as soon as possible. As a result, we put out new banknote series with enhanced security features on a regular basis. New series of banknotes with new security features are put into circulation every 15 years or so. A $10 banknote from 1973, the first note with a metallic security stripe. It was designed to make counterfeiting more difficult.

This $10 note from 1989 has enhanced security features and better security inks to make it harder to counterfeit.

In 2004, the $100 note was Canada’s first bank note with a metallic holographic stripe. The next series of bank notes, to begin in 2019, will have even more security features. Counterfeiters are working harder than ever to fake these new notes. That’s why we are also working hard to make bank notes even safer. And that’s why you can be sure the money in your wallet is safe and secure. The Bank of Canada’s commitment to cash

The Bank is continually working to ensure that our bank notes are durable and readily accepted and that Canadians have confidence in them. The Bank knows that retailers prefer bank notes too, because they are easy to use, easy to store and easy to check for authenticity. That’s why we make it easier for Canadians to use cash—and retailers to accept it. We provide secure fencing for existing bank note depots and we are building two new ones, so that we can deliver more cash where it is needed. We are also developing new equipment that would process notes faster and more efficiently. The Bank will also explore new technology that will extend the lifespan of lower-denomination bank notes. We are committed to giving Canadians access to the high-quality notes they need. The Bank of Canada’s commitment to accessible bank notes

Our bank notes are national symbols and they are a way for Canadians to express their pride in their country. So, we make sure that images on the note are accessible to everyone. This means that the images we choose should be available to people who are sight-impaired, and respect Canada’s official languages. We also want to make it easier for everyone to find cash and to use cash. The Bank of Canada’s commitment to the environment

The Bank’s commitment to cash also includes a commitment to the environment. We have developed more sustainable bank notes. This means that the notes are more durable and will last longer. We also use greener materials and work with suppliers who adhere to sound environmental practices. These practices include recycling, overall reductions in water and energy used, and eliminating the use of toxic substances. Bank Note Launch

The Bank of Canada releases a new bank note series every few years. The new series includes new designs with images and security features you can see, and some you can only feel. The themes explored on the notes are meaningful to Canadians. The themes, as well as the images that represent them, are chosen from different periods in Canada’s history. These images are seen in many places where Canadians live and work. You may recognize some of the images and themes from your school textbook or from stories your parents or grandparents have told you. The new series of bank notes also includes images of Canada’s culture and society today. So, the notes reflect Canada’s history and the way Canadians live and work today. The new notes are better for the environment. They last longer, and the green ink is produced using natural, non-toxic components. The polymer material is also recyclable. And, the notes are easy to use, because they are waterproof, durable and easy to check for authenticity. The new notes are also better for Canadians. They are safer and more cost-effective. They are also accessible for everyone, including people who are sight-impaired. The new notes will be released over time. The first new note, the $10, was released on June 20, 2017. The new $10 note features the Canadian icebreaker CCGS Amundsen. The Amundsen helps keep shipping lanes open in the Arctic, and is used to explore the Arctic. The Amundsen has been used in several important research projects, and has helped scientists study climate change, oceans and ice. The next new note, the $5, will be released later this year.
